lead.hed: DVIDS: Destroyer Carl M. Levin ran a live-fire drill in the Western Pacific
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Wednesday morning: sailors on USS Carl M. Levin (DDG-120) prepared to fire an M240 machine gun during a live-fire training exercise while underway in the Western Pacific on Sept. 22. The ship is forward-deployed with Destroyer Squadron 15, the Navy's largest destroyer squadron and 7th Fleet's principal surface force. Training evolution, not a combat report.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Isabelle Dial · DVIDS 9959741 · Public domain · Boatswain's Mate Seaman Davieon Cooper prepares to fire an M240 aboard USS Carl M. Levin (DDG 120), Western Pacific, Sept. 22, 2026.

political.hed: USNI: Navy public works teams move under Installations Command
political.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: Navy public works maintenance teams will now sit under Commander, Navy Installations Command instead of Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command. The sea service said the move puts about 10,000 civilian and military personnel under the direct authority of base commanding officers, to speed base maintenance. Reorganization, not a new ship.

political.hed: Defense News: Destroyers in the Middle East are being tested as demand mounts
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: the concentration of Navy destroyers in the Middle East raises questions about meeting sustained operational demand. Reporting on force posture, not a new deployment order.

political.hed: Heritage: Five drone lessons from Ukraine for NATO's northeastern flank
political.insight: Heritage Foundation, Tuesday: a defense report argues Ukrainian forces have shown how drones used as sensors, munitions, and platforms can offset a larger military, and draws five lessons for NATO's northeastern flank. Report, not a U.S. statute.

tech.hed: USNI: U.S. and Britain launched a Mk 48 from the Royal Navy's unmanned sub
tech.insight: USNI News, Tuesday: the U.S. and U.K. test-launched a torpedo from a Royal Navy extra-large unmanned underwater vehicle as a proof-of-concept trial for AUKUS Pillar 2. On Sept. 13, XV Excalibur launched a U.S. Mk 48 heavyweight torpedo at the British Underwater Test and Evaluation Centre in Scotland. Proof of concept, not a deployed weapon.

tech.hed: Defense News: CENTCOM has become a battle lab for unmanned systems
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: unmanned systems have moved from exercises into an active war. After a U.S. Army helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz in June, a Navy unmanned vessel helped recover two service members. A month later, CENTCOM said three Corsair sea drones struck a submarine and ship maintenance facility at Bandar Abbas — the first time American forces employed sea drones in combat. Field use, not a procurement decision.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Winslett says culture, not just hearings, decides what gets built
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Wednesday: Gary Winslett argues that NIMBY politics is not only a prisoner's dilemma of self-interest and public hearings. Culture decides whether building is the default or the deviant move, who has standing to object, and whether a new development looks like a contribution or a threat. Forum essay, not a zoning vote.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Bahnsen and Shelton on conservatism's fault line
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Wednesday: Mitchell Bahnsen and John Shelton review a collection edited by Joseph Prud'homme on what conservatism is willing, and unwilling, to do to restore the common good. They contrast Burkean prudence with counter-revolutionary tactics. Book review, not a party platform.
